newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police and military authorities have thrown a security blanket over the city for United States' President Bill Clinton who is due tonight for a 27-hour state visit. Army bomb disposal squads have conducted a final round of inspection and police dogs were mobilised for random checks of areas through which the presidential motorcade will pass during his brief but busy visit. (BANGKOK POST).

- The trade in drugs, arms, contraband, smuggled oil, cheap labour and sex threatenS the long-term economic stability of Thailand, Chulalongkorn University researchers have warned. They say the illegal businesses are together worth 600-800 billion baht a year - 15-18 percent of the country's gross national product. And they corrupt the political process and lead to such ills as vote-buying. (BANGKOK POST)

- Saxophonist Art Porter, who arrived in Bankok on Wednesday to join 40 other jazz musicians in celebrating the 50th anniversary of His Majesty the King's accession to the throne, has died in an accident. Porter and two Thais drowned on Saturday after their overloaded boat capsized while crossing an agricultural reservoir in Kanchanaburi province. (THE NATION)

- Thailand's air freight services will be a key sector to benefit from the scheduled signing with the United States of a treaty ending double taxation. An agreement on nine points is expected to be signed during the state visit of President Bill Clinton. (BANGKOK POST)

- Germany's largest independent power producer Steag is planning to invest US$150-200 million for the setting up five power plants in Southeast Asia and Taiwan in the next five years, its first investment outside Germany. The company plans to invest in Southeast Asia, investing in production capacity of 100 megawatts a year for the next five years, on a company's equity basis of 25 percent. (THE NATION)

- The Cabinet is to postpone its plans to reduce import duty on petro-chemical products for another one more year, saying that the reduction will affect more than 60 related products. The Cabinet will meet on Tuesday and is expected to postpone the duty reduction plans to January 1, 1998 from January 1, 1997. (MANAGER)
